newsitem.title: FRANCE: DHL rules out Belfort as Rhine Valley hub.
newsitem.headline: DHL rules out Belfort as Rhine Valley hub.

text.p: DHL Worldwide Express said a former NATO airfield at Belfort-Fontaine, in eastern France, had never been in the running as the location of its proposed Rhine Valley hub.
French press reports said a march, last Saturday, June 14, a march against DHL developing its activities at the airfield was held in Belfort attracting around 8,000 people.

"We can confirm that the Belfort-Fontaine airfield does not figure in our plans and never has done and for two simple reasons - it is currently not in service as an airfield and would require considerable investment to put into working order," DHL's Brussels-based Corporate Affairs spokesman, Guy Collette, told Reuters.
He said DHL had been approached by public authorities in the Belfort area "some time ago" on developing the airfield but no formal discussions had ensued.

Last summer, Strasbourg-Entzheim airport was all set to emerge as DHL's Rhine Valley air cargo hub when the project collapsed amid protests by residents and political leaders over potential night-time noise.

Following the opposition to the Strasbourg project, DHL has been looking at several sites in the Alsace-Lorraine region and the other side of the Rhine, in Germany, including existing or former miltary airfields and commerical airports.
"We are not prepared to reveal the identity of the sites under consideration suffice to say it'll probably be three months before we make our choice," Collette added.
He said DHL continued to work closely with the French government, including the Defence and Transport Ministries, on the project.
"What is uppermost for us in the choice of site is that we have the backing and support of all the relevant authorities concerned."
The service level of DHL business had not suffered as a result of delays in setting up a Rhine Valley hub.
"As with all our regional hubs, it is viewed as long-term investment and our existing network has enabled us to absorb "Rhine Valley" traffic."
A Defence Ministry spokesman told Reuters that a soon-to-be decommissioned military airfield at Toul-Rosieres was "still on offer" to DHL.
"Frankly, at present, Toul-Rosieres is the only site "on the table" although we gather it is not an ideal location for DHL."

Commenting on potential, working, miltary airfields, he added: "We would not be against DHL locating at Colmar-Meyenheim, for example but it is hard to see state funding being made available for the necessary restructuring of the site for commerical activities."

He said there was a possibility DHL's Rhine Valley project would be discussed by France's new ministers for Defence, Transport and Regional Development between now and end-June. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
